Hon'ble Alok Mathur,J.
1. Heard Sri Chitranshu Srivastav, learned counsel for the applicant and the learned A.G.A. for the respondents.

2. By means of the present 482 Cr.P.C. petition the applicant has challenged the entire proceedings of sessions trial No.321 of 2022 (Session Case No.478 of 2022) arising out of case crime No.0594 of 2021 under Sections- 498A, 304 B, 323, 201 IPC and 3/4 of Dowry Prohibition Act, 1961, police station Sardhana, District Meerut.

According to the first information report which was lodged by father-in-law of the applicant on 5.9.2021 it was alleged that the applicant had married the daughter of the complainant on 5.3.2016 according to Hindu rites and rituals and in the marriage he had Deepak Jain Nirala vs State Of U.P. sentences.text: Subsequently, it was alleged that the applicant and the family members did not allow the complainant to meet his daughter and subsequently it was found that she was missing and could not be found and accordingly the first information report has been lodged.

3. From the aforesaid, it is clear that the daughter of the complainant and wife of the applicant is missing since a long time and having been married to the applicant it was incumbent upon him to have disclosed the whereabouts of his wife.
The investigation was concluded and charge sheet was filed and the trial is proceeding where the charges have been framed against the applicant on 17.4.2022.

The only alibi taken by the petitioner for assailing the proceedings are that one NCR has been lodged at Police Station Nayi Mandi, District Muzaffarnagar which has been registered by one Roovi Gupta on 23.8.2021.

It has been submitted that the NCR has been lodged by the same person,
who is alleged to be wife of the applicant.
The said NCR does not in any manner absolves or lessens the offence of the applicant but in any way these facts will be looked into by the trial court.
4. No other ground was raised by the applicant assailing the proceedings before the trial court.
5. I do not find any merits in this 482 Cr.P.C. petition, which is hereby dismissed.

(Alok Mathur, J.) Order Date :- 7.2.2025 RKM.
